mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which typically leads to stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth is positive, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 growth is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS > 4.5% is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 1.5% annualized and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3.0% annualized, the market perceives a sustainable economic expansion without inflationary pressures, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both GDPC1 growth > 1.5% and CPIAUCSL < 3.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%), the economy is overheating with high interest rates and a tight labor market, increasing recession risk and triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by employment growth exceeding 0.5% in three months (PAYEMS), signals robust economic conditions and rising consumer spending, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS growth > 0.5% is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects stronger manufacturing and supply chain activity, which correlates with rising corporate output and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC for INDPRO growth is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in CPI inflation above 5.0% annualized within three months (CPIAUCSL) triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL > 5.0% is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint growth of housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) above 0.3% and 0.2% annualized, respectively, indicates robust household demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST growth > 0.3% and RSAFS growth > 0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS growth exceed thresholds, or the Rank IC for the interaction condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
